sentiment.rationale: Full-year revenue guidance was raised by 75 bps to 3.75%-4.75% growth, and adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $2.52-$2.62, while adjusted operating income guidance was maintained. The guidance raise is organic, driven by strong sales and share gains, not attributed to one-time items. However, the maintained operating income guidance despite the revenue raise, combined with significant cost headwinds from general liability claims and tariff uncertainty, prevents a higher score.

summary.revenue: Total revenues of $177.4 billion, up 4.8% reported, up 5.6% in constant currency. Net sales of $175.75 billion, up 4.8%.
summary.eps: GAAP EPS of $0.88, up 57.1% year-over-year. Adjusted EPS of $0.68, up 1.5% year-over-year.
summary.guidance: Q3 FY26: net sales growth (cc) 3.75%-4.75%, operating income growth (cc) 3.0%-6.0%, adjusted EPS $0.58-$0.60. Full-year FY26: net sales growth (cc) raised to 3.75%-4.75% (from 3.0%-4.0%), adjusted operating income growth (cc) maintained at 3.5%-5.5%, adjusted EPS raised to $2.52-$2.62 (from $2.50-$2.60).
summary.margin: Consolidated gross margin rate increased 4 bps to 24.5% (up 9 bps adjusted). Adjusted SG&A deleveraged 35 bps to 21.0% of net sales. Adjusted EBITDA margin decreased ~10 bps to 6.5%.
key_risks: Higher self-insured general liability claims expense: $450 million incremental in Q2, 560 bps headwind to adjusted operating income growth.
Tariff-related cost pressures: costs increasing each week, expected to continue into Q3 and Q4; uncertainty around final tariff resolution.
Merchandise category mix headwind: grocery and health & wellness sales outpacing general merchandise, pressuring gross margin.
Currency exchange rate fluctuations: $1.5 billion negative impact on revenue in Q2; expected modest headwind to reported sales in Q3.
Uncertain demand backdrop: consumer behavior adjustments in middle and lower income households; potential for unit sales to slow.
key_opportunities: eCommerce growth: global eCommerce sales up 25%, with all segments exceeding 20% growth; Walmart U.S. eCommerce up 26%.
Higher-margin business growth: global advertising up 46% (including VIZIO), Walmart Connect up 31%; membership income up 15% globally.
Market share gains: gaining share in the US and across international markets; upper-income households contributing largest gains.
AI and technology investments: new AI acceleration role, development of super-agents (Sparky, associate, supplier, developer agents).
Supply chain automation and speed: store-fulfilled delivery growing nearly 50%; 95% of US households to have dynamic delivery windows by year-end.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Management expresses confidence in the business model and strategy, stating 'we're positioned to win' and 'we feel good about the back half of the year,' while acknowledging uncertainty and maintaining flexibility.
